verdict.rationale: React's own repository describes this capability almost word for word: build encapsulated components that manage their own state, then compose them into complex UIs. The docs back this up, describing components as UI pieces with their own logic, composed into screens, pages and apps, and DevTools can edit props and state. missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the local-state mechanism (e.g., state hook reference) in the pack, independent hands-on corroboration of component state and composition.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build encapsulated components that manage their own local state and compose them into complex UIs

citations.quote: Build encapsulated components that manage their own state, then compose them to make complex UIs.
A component is a piece of the UI (user interface) that has its own logic and appearance.
Create your own React components like `Thumbnail`, `LikeButton`, and `Video`. Then combine them into entire screens, pages, and apps.
Use React Developer Tools to inspect React components, edit props and state, and identify performance problems.
